Question
========
In a fully associative cache, what do two addresses that are in conflict share?


Answerlist
----------
* Index
* Tag
* Offset
* Address size

Solution
========
A fully associative cache has no row index: an address is split into a tag and an offset only. Two addresses collide when they have the same tag, that is when they designate the same block.

Answerlist
----------
* 0. A fully associative cache has no index bits at all.
* 1. With no index, the tag is the whole block address, so conflicting addresses share their tag.
* 0. The offset selects a byte inside the line and plays no role in placement.
* 0. All addresses have the same size; this says nothing about a conflict.
